maria: Heads-up — I'm adding a short deprecation note for legacy quant profiles in the Optimize toolkit docs. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/472. Need a quick sanity check on the migration helper snippet and that all links target the new /optimize/quantization page. cc @jon @ashu :wave:

jon: on it. can you paste the exact snippet you want in the PR? will check SDK v2 call names. also can we add a small example of expected output after migration?

maria: snippet is in the PR under /docs/optimize/migration.md — but it's still using old `optkit.quant_profile` keys. here's the current pseudo-snippet in the PR:

```python
# legacy-ish profile -> new schema (toy example)
old = {"bits": 8, "per_channel": False, "fallback": "fp16"}
# TODO: transform to new `quant` structure
```

ashu: saw the PR, thanks. FYI CI is failing because the internal link `/docs/optimize/quant-profiles` 404s (we renamed the page). that link is in the migration.md and in the table-of-contents file. i'll fix both.

kevin: quick helper that might be useful to include in the docs (keeps example minimal):

```python
def migrate_legacy_quant(old_profile):
    # map legacy keys to new schema keys we use in Optimize toolkit v2
    new = {
        "quant": {
            "mode": "int8" if old_profile.get("bits") == 8 else "fp16",
            "channelwise": bool(old_profile.get("per_channel")),
            "fallback": old_profile.get("fallback", "fp16")
        }
    }
    return new

# example usage
# migrate_legacy_quant({"bits":8, "per_channel":False, "fallback":"fp16"})
```

jon: nice — we'll change call names: use `optimize.quantize_profile` in the docs snippet so it matches SDK v2. I'll push that change into your branch, @maria.

ashu: i've fixed the 404s in a tiny commit, running linkchecker now. if it passes i'll push and request a re-run of CI. the TOC had an old slug.

taylor: small doc suggestion — add a one-line note about batch-size rounding interactions with quantization. a lot of customers see worse latency if they blindly increase batch size after quantizing. suggest a sentence + pointer to perf playbook.

maria: good call, @taylor — add a one-liner under "Migration notes" and link to /optimize/perf-playbook. keep it short.

docs-bot: Build started for docs/pull/472 • checks: linkcheck, lint, mkdocs-build

jon: i've updated the SDK snippet and added expected input/output for the helper. also switched to `optimize.migrations.migrate_quant_profile(old)` so it's more discoverable in the API reference. pushed to the PR.

ashu: linkcheck passed locally, rerunning CI now.

kevin: opened a tiny helper PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/476) that contains the `migrate_legacy_quant` utility and a unit test. can we land it as a follow-up and reference it from the migration doc?

maria: yes — let's merge migration doc and link to the helper PR (or land helper first). priority is to avoid leaving broken links.

docs-bot: Build succeeded for docs/pull/472 (linkcheck, lint, mkdocs-build)

maria: thanks everyone — i'll do a final pass and merge once the helper reference is added. aiming to merge by EOD if no regressions. :green_heart:

jon: happy to own the helper reference update.

ashu: i'll watch for any followups in the TOC indexing.

kevin: cool — will rebase my helper PR onto main after your merge.

maria: awesome. closing the loop here — thanks for the quick reviews and patches. if anything else pops up tag me or open an issue in the repo. :sparkles:
